dedupe_keys.name: nina interactive green roof prioritisation app for oslo earth engine mcda

description: This web application lets stakeholders run a spatial multi-criteria decision analysis of where retrofitting green roofs in Oslo would deliver the most needed ecosystem services, using Google Earth Engine cloud computing so that the analysis is openly accessible. It covers buildings across Oslo, Norway, weighting temperature regulation, stormwater runoff mitigation, habitat for biodiversity, aesthetic value and noise reduction according to preference profiles of green roof designers, owners and operators for different building types; the study found strong spatial correlation in ecosystem service deficits, so different preferences still point to common target areas. It was developed by Zander Venter, David Barton and co-authors and described in Ecosystem Services in August 2021, where the authors present it as a generalisable tool for engaging stakeholders in planning nature-based solutions. Licence: not stated for the resource; the describing article (doi:10.1016/j.ecoser.2021.101314) is CC-BY-4.0. Access is free of charge. Caveats: it is built for Oslo, and the ecosystem service layers are fixed by the study. It supports siting of green roofs as green-blue infrastructure for stormwater and heat adaptation; a related record is Roofpedia.
